title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation tool was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery of a real person without her knowledge or permission. The person using the tool obtained source photographs from the victim's social media accounts and generated fake explicit images, then distributed them through multiple anonymous accounts across social platforms. This represents a straightforward misuse of deployed technology by someone who obtained access to it.

The failure happened at the point of deployment. AI image generation systems are available to the public without controls that would prevent this use case. The system itself has no mechanism to detect when it is being asked to create non-consensual intimate imagery or to refuse such requests. It has no way to verify the consent of people depicted in source images.

What would have caught this is either technical controls built into the system to reject requests for non-consensual intimate imagery, or human review of outputs before they were released to users. It is not established whether the tool used had any such safeguards, or whether they were bypassed or absent.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading sexually explicit images of a college acquaintance using artificial intelligence technology. Bansal obtained photos from the woman's private social media accounts and used AI tools to generate obscene morphed images, which he then circulated through fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while maintaining anonymity with multiple Gmail addresses.

The victim, also 22 years old, reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving messages from anonymous accounts informing her that the manipulated images and videos were being shared. Police conducted a detailed digital investigation, analyzing social media accounts and email trails to identify Bansal. During questioning, he admitted to knowing the woman from college and having developed personal resentment toward her following past conflicts. The investigation is continuing, and police recovered a mobile phone, SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case.
